questions.question: The first Anglo - Afghan war took place between 1838 - ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1842**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Anglo-Afghan War** took place between **1838 and 1842**.
 
• It was a conflict between the **British East India Company** and the **Afghan Empire**.
 
• The war was initiated by the British as part of their strategy to establish a buffer state in Afghanistan to counter the influence of the Russian Empire.
 
• It is also referred to as the **First Afghan War**.
 
• The war ended disastrously for the British with a significant defeat during the retreat from Kabul in January 1842, where only a single European, Dr. William Brydon, reached Jalalabad.
 
• The British forces later regrouped and re-entered Kabul in September 1842 to rescue prisoners and exact revenge before withdrawing from Afghanistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **British East India Company**

 
 
• The British East India Company was a private company with a royal charter to trade in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It played a significant role in the colonization of India and was a major force in the expansion of British influence in Asia.
 
• It was dissolved in 1874 after the British Crown took direct control of India following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
 
 
• **Afghan Empire**
 
 
• The Afghan Empire, also known as the Durrani Empire, was founded by Ahmad Shah Durrani in 1747.
 
• It covered present-day Afghanistan, parts of Iran, Pakistan, and India.
 
• The empire played a central role in the geopolitical struggles of the 18th and 19th centuries in the region.
 
 
 
• **Dr. William Brydon**
 
 
• Dr. William Brydon was an assistant surgeon in the British East India Company Army.
 
• He is famously known as the sole European survivor of the retreat from Kabul during the First Anglo-Afghan War.
 
• His survival and account of the retreat became emblematic of the war's disastrous outcome for the British.

questions.question: What is the full form of GST?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is an indirect tax used in India on the supply of goods and services.
 
• It is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that is levied on every value addition.
 
• GST has subsumed many indirect taxes that were previously levied by the central and state governments, such as excise duty, VAT, and service tax.
 
• The GST Council is responsible for making recommendations to the Union and State Governments on issues related to GST.
 
• GST is categorized into three types: **CGST (Central GST)**, **SGST (State GST)**, and **IGST (Integrated GST)**.
 
• GST was implemented in India on **1st July 2017**.
 
• The primary goal of GST is to create a unified market and eliminate the cascading effect of taxes on the economy.

questions.question: How many fundamental duties of citizens have been enumerated by the 42nd Amendment of the Constitution, adopted in 1976?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment** of the Indian Constitution was adopted in **1976**.
 
• This amendment introduced a new part, **Part IV-A**, which contains the **Fundamental Duties** of citizens.
 
• Initially, there were **10 Fundamental Duties** enumerated in this part.
 
• These duties are inspired by the **Constitution of the USSR** and aim to promote a sense of **patriotism and unity** among citizens.
 
• The 10 Fundamental Duties include respecting the Constitution, the National Flag, and the National Anthem, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, and upholding and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India, among others.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while they enjoy their rights, they also have responsibilities towards their nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

​The fundamental duties of the Indian Constitution are listed in Article 51A of Part IV A of the Constitution. They include: 

__
 
• Abiding by the Constitution 
 
• Respecting the Constitution's ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem 
 
• Protecting the country's sovereignty, unity, and integrity 
 
• Defending the country and rendering national service when called upon 
 
• Protecting and improving the natural environment 
 
• Developing a scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform 
 
• Safeguarding public property and abjuring violence 
 
• Striving towards excellence in all spheres of activity 
 
• **11th Fundamental Duty**__
 
 
• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the **86th Amendment Act** in **2002**.
 
• In 2002, Article 51(k) was added to include the duty to provide free and compulsory education to children between the ages of 6 and 14.
 
• This duty mandates that parents or guardians provide opportunities for education to their children between the ages of 6 and 14 years.

questions.question: What balances the atmospheric pressure with equal force so that animals do not crumble under the high pressure exerted on them by the atmosphere?

options.text: Energy produced by the food consumed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blood Pressure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood pressure** is the force exerted by circulating blood on the walls of blood vessels.
 
• This pressure is crucial for maintaining the flow of blood throughout the body, ensuring that oxygen and nutrients reach various tissues and organs.
 
• Blood pressure is measured using two values: **systolic pressure** (when the heart beats) and **diastolic pressure** (when the heart is at rest).
 
• The human body has evolved to maintain blood pressure at levels that balance the external atmospheric pressure, preventing the body from collapsing under its weight.
 
• Proper regulation of blood pressure is essential for overall health and well-being, and imbalances can lead to conditions such as hypertension or hypotension.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Moon's gravitational pull**__

 __
 
• The Moon's gravitational pull affects the Earth primarily through tides in the oceans.
 
• This gravitational force is too weak to have any significant impact on counteracting atmospheric pressure on animals.
 
 
 
• **Pressure because of sunlight**__
 __
 
• Sunlight exerts radiation pressure, but this force is negligible compared to atmospheric pressure.
 
• It does not play a role in balancing the atmospheric pressure on animals.
 
 
 
• **Energy produced by the food consumed**__
 
 
• The energy from food is used by the body for various functions, including movement and metabolism.
 
• It does not directly balance atmospheric pressure on the body.

__
 
• **Kalindi** is not a major river basin in India.
 
• It is often confused with rivers like the **Yamuna**, which is also known as Kalindi in some contexts, but it is not recognized as a separate major river basin.
 
• Major river basins in India include significant rivers like the **Ganges, Brahmaputra, Indus, Godavari, Krishna, and Mahanadi**.
 
• These major river basins cover extensive geographical areas and play crucial roles in irrigation, drinking water supply, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• The importance of a river basin is typically determined by its **size, length, and the population it supports**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Narmada**__

 __
 
• The **Narmada** River is one of the major rivers in central India.
 
• It flows westwards over a length of 1,312 km before draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The river flows through the states of **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Krishna**__
 __
 
• The **Krishna** River is one of the longest rivers in India, with a length of about 1,400 km.
 
• It originates in the **Western Ghats** near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.
 
• The river flows through **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Tapi**__
 
 
• The **Tapi** River, also known as the Tapti, is a river in central India.

questions.question: What is the function of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **endoplasmic reticulum (ER)** is a critical organelle in eukaryotic cells, involved in various cellular processes.
 
• The ER is classified into two types: **rough ER (RER)** and **smooth ER (SER)**.
 
• **Smooth ER (SER)** is primarily involved in **lipid synthesis and detoxification** of drugs and poisons.
 
• The SER is also important for the **metabolism of carbohydrates** and the regulation of calcium concentration.
 
• **Rough ER (RER)**, on the other hand, is studded with ribosomes and is mainly involved in **protein synthesis**.
 
• The ER works closely with the **Golgi apparatus** to modify, sort, and package proteins and lipids for secretion or use within the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DNA replication**__

 __
 
• DNA replication is the process by which a cell duplicates its DNA before cell division.
 
• This process primarily occurs in the **nucleus of eukaryotic cells**.
 
• The enzymes involved in DNA replication include **DNA polymerase, helicase, and ligase**.
 
• It is a critical process for **genetic continuity** and cell proliferation.
 
 
 
• **Energy production**__
 __
 
• Energy production in cells is primarily carried out by **mitochondria**.
 
• Mitochondria are known as the **"powerhouses of the cell"** because they generate **ATP (adenosine triphosphate)**, the cell's main energy currency.
 
• This process of energy production is called **cellular respiration**.
 
 
 
• **Protein synthesis**__
 
 
• Protein synthesis occurs primarily in the **rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER)** and the **cytoplasm**.
 
• Ribosomes on the RER translate **messenger RNA (mRNA)** into proteins.
 
• These proteins are then modified and transported to their destinations within or outside the cell.

• Slow motion is a term used to describe the speed of an object.
 
• It does not describe the nature of the path taken by the stones.

• **Mitochondria** are known as the **powerhouses of the cell** because they generate the primary energy molecule, **ATP (adenosine triphosphate)**.
 
• They are double-membraned organelles found in the cytoplasm of almost all eukaryotic cells.
 
• **ATP** is produced through a process called **cellular respiration**, which occurs in the mitochondria.
 
• Mitochondria have their own **DNA**, which is separate from the nuclear DNA, allowing them to produce some of their own proteins.
 
• The inner membrane of mitochondria is folded into structures called **cristae**, which increase the surface area for ATP production.
 
• Mitochondria play a crucial role in regulating the metabolic activity of the cell.

• The rough ER is involved in **protein synthesis** and the smooth ER is associated with **lipid synthesis** and **detoxification** processes.
 
 
 
• **Cell Wall**__
 __
 
• The **cell wall** is a rigid layer found outside the cell membrane in plants, fungi, and certain prokaryotes.
 
• It provides **structural support** and **protection** to the cell.
 
• In plants, the cell wall is primarily composed of **cellulose**.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles**__
 
 
• **Vacuoles** are membrane-bound organelles that are present in both animal and plant cells, though they are more prominent in plant cells.
 
• They are primarily involved in **storage** and can contain water, nutrients, or waste products.
 
• In plant cells, the central vacuole also helps in maintaining **turgor pressure** against the cell wall.

questions.question: Sometimes when heated, solid changes into liquid at normal atmospheric pressure on reaching its melting point. What is the name of the amount of heat required?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Latent heat of fusion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Latent heat of fusion** is the amount of heat required to convert a solid into a liquid at its melting point without changing its temperature.
 
• This process involves breaking the **intermolecular forces** that hold the solid together.
 
• During this phase transition, the temperature of the substance remains constant.
 
• The energy absorbed as latent heat of fusion is used to change the state of the substance rather than increasing its temperature.
 
• Examples include the melting of ice to water and the melting of metals for casting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Latent heat of diffusion**__

 __
 
• This is not a commonly recognized term in thermodynamics.
 
• **Diffusion** generally refers to the movement of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration, not a phase change.
 
 
 
• **Latent melting point**__
 __
 
• This term is incorrect because the **melting point** is a specific temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid, not a measure of heat.
 
 
 
• **Latent change of state point**__
 
 
• This term is not scientifically accurate. The correct terms are **latent heat of fusion** for solid to liquid and **latent heat of vaporization** for liquid to gas.
